result.title: The Sense Paradigm for World Models
result.summary: Latent world models predict the future in an embedding space rather than in pixels. An encoder trained only to predict collapses and maps every observation to the same point, so existing models add a mechanism against collapse, such as a target network, a variance penalty or a distribution penalty. These mechanisms keep the embedding from collapsing, but they leave its distances without meaning, and the model cannot tell a reversible transition from an irreversible one. We propose Sense, a single cross-entropy loss over the directed distance $d(x\to y)=\sum_i \mathrm{ReLU}(y_i-x_i)$ that replaces these mechanisms. The loss avoids collapse on its own, and since the encoder no longer needs the predictor, the predictor is fitted afterwards to fixed embeddings by plain regression. On four pixel environments, the return distance learned by Sense detects irreversible transitions with an AUC between 0.95 and 1.00, where LeWorldModel stays between 0.39 and 0.59. On TwoRoom, the navigation benchmark of LeWorldModel, planning with Sense reaches the goal in 100% of episodes against 91% for LeWorldModel. As the goal moves farther away, the planning failure rate of every baseline grows, while that of Sense stays near zero in Cup, Cliff and Sokoban and is the lowest of all methods in Pendulum.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Sense，用建立在有向距离上的单一交叉熵损失替代目标网络、方差惩罚或分布惩罚等防坍缩机制，训练潜空间世界模型的编码器，并将预测器事后回归拟合；在四个像素环境中检验不可逆转移识别与规划表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单一损失即可防表示坍缩并让潜距离承载可解释语义」的做法，可能为 LVR 中的信息坍缩诊断、latent 相似度是否保留任务状态差异及转移可逆性提供方法线索，尚需核查该几何在视觉推理状态上的适用性。
